habitats: Unflooded upper lava tubes receiving organic debris
Sunken-cave splash debris above prolonged immersion
summary: A nonphotosynthetic decomposer fruits as pale cushions on damp, oxygenated organic deposits. Dark-tube colonies require imported carbon and remain confined to aerated substrate. Accessible mature cushions offer edible fungal tissue and a sticky spore-bearing surface to ecolumbre and babosa, allowing local contact dispersal between suitable deposits. Coastal colonies occupy freshwater-flushed debris above prolonged tidal immersion and emit no light (F9, F23, F24).

chains.trait: Digestive filaments in aerated organic deposits
links: Litter, carcass fragments and transported debris provide chemical energy.
Filaments digest material externally and absorb breakdown products.
Moisture and oxygen support growth without daylight.
Carbon-starved rock and permanently anaerobic pools exclude colonies.
chains.play: Trace a dark-cave patch to its imported organic substrate without treating its presence as proof of safe air.
chains.weakness: Colonies fail when carbon or moisture runs out, under prolonged seawater immersion or in permanently anaerobic H₂S pools.
observe: Pale threads penetrate softened organic debris.
Growth ends at clean bare rock.
Cushions stop above a stagnant pool rather than covering its submerged floor.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Dark growth consumes imported organic carbon and requires a suitable oxygenated substrate. Explicitly exclude permanently anaerobic pools and prolonged immersion; an unflooded tube can still contain humid substrate. Strict review (2026-11-19): Residual: Organic substrates supply energy, and external digestion explains nonphotosynthetic growth. F9 provides the cave setting and F24 permits compatible organic food. Residual weakness: oxygenated substrate is necessary but does not establish tolerance of sea salts or toxic vent deposits under F20 and F23; aeration also does not guarantee air safe for visiting creatures.

analogues.mechanism: Extracellular digestion and absorption support growth on organic substrates without photosynthesis.

chains.trait: Edible cushions with contact-transfer spore patches
links: Mature cushions expose a moist, tacky spore layer beside edible tissue in sheltered organic deposits.
Ecolumbre and babosa encounter and consume suitable fungal tissue within their documented habitats, receiving a food reward.
Contact leaves viable spore clumps on ecolumbre's mouth or feet and in babosa's surface mucus without requiring survival through digestion.
Later contact with another damp, aerated organic deposit rubs off some clumps, allowing establishment where carbon and oxygen suffice.
Contact transport supplements airborne dispersal across sheltered litter surfaces where weak air movement makes direct spore delivery patchy.
chains.play: Watch fungal grazers acquire sticky spore clumps and follow their local movement between organic patches; deep colonies need no rondo visits.
chains.weakness: Most transported spores reach unsuitable surfaces, drying reduces viability, and neither animal movement nor airborne spores can establish colonies on carbon-starved rock.
observe: A mature cushion has a tacky tan spore patch beside pale edible tissue.
After feeding, ecolumbre carries clumps around its mouth or feet, or babosa leaves spore-bearing mucus at the cushion edge.
A later contact leaves a clump on damp litter; a small new colony develops there if the deposit remains aerated.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Rondo is an occasional sampler and spore carrier, not a staple fungivore. Fruit mimicry is a fictional specialization; deep colonies cannot assume visits from an inaccessible surface animal. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: The original chain depended on unrewarded herbivore investigation and unexplained muzzle transfer; the rewrite uses rewarded fungal consumers and explicit external attachment and deposition. Residual: Both named consumers have fungal diets and overlapping habitats, so encounter and feeding require no dietary revision. F9 supplies suitable cave architecture; F24 permits compatible biochemistry but does not establish adhesive spores or successful transport. External transfer avoids assuming digestive survival. Residual weaknesses are attachment versus subsequent release, viability in babosa's alkaloid-rich mucus, and transfer before grooming or drying. These remain conditional biological specializations, not contradictions: the chain explicitly requires viable clumps, suitable deposits and local contact, and does not claim universal establishment or exclusive animal dispersal.

analogues.mechanism: The supplied truffle example supports animal attraction and ingestion-based transport, not external attachment. Tacky clumps transferred by documented fungal consumers are an explicit fictional contact-dispersal specialization; wind remains a supplementary route.

food_for: ecolumbre grazes suitable fresh fungal tissue in aerated organic-fed patches.
babosa consumes soft cushions and decomposing litter.
gameplay.gift_item: A fresh humus cushion from clean aerated litter for ecolumbre.

poison.signal: Pale tissue lacks an alkaloid warning; substrate contamination and decay remain separate concerns.

gameplay.notes: Fresh fungal tissue is distinct from its decomposing substrate. Rondo is not a required consumer or disperser. Coastal colonies require freshwater-flushed substrate and adequate aeration; neither pale cushions nor oxygenated substrate certify safe cave air. Bodies reflect light and never glow. Small tissue fragments or edible microbial aggregates may enter tidal water from occupied sunken-cave fringe deposits, but this is an incidental input.

relations.note: Grazes suitable fresh tissue in aerated organic-fed cave patches and can incidentally transfer sticky spores between deposits.
Consumes soft cushions and decomposing litter; viable spores in external mucus may be deposited on later substrate contacts.

At occupied freshwater-flushed sunken-cave fringe deposits, tidal splash can detach small edible tissue fragments or microbial aggregates that enter the flooded tube and are occasionally intercepted by its mucus net.
Occasionally intercepts small suspended tissue fragments or edible microbial aggregates washed from occupied sunken-cave fringe deposits into adjacent tidal water.
Decomposes shed fronds in suitable humid deposits.
Shares some aerated entrance deposits while remaining nonluminous.

generator.trunk: No trunk; clustered fleshy cushions emerge over substrate filaments.

branching.buttress: None; branching describes substrate filaments, while visible bodies are rounded cushion clusters.

leaf.type: None; rounded porous fruiting surface with localized tacky spore patches
leaf.arrangement: Loose cushion groups over organic material

overlay_rules: Mature spore patches become tacky tan areas.
Waterlogged or spent cushions darken and collapse.
Fresh hydrated cushion margins remain pale and rounded.

placement.slope: Protected litter floors, debris-catching benches and ledges above stagnant pools.
placement.wetness: Humid oxygenated substrate without prolonged immersion. Exclude persistently hypoxic, anaerobic or H₂S-bearing deposits. Coastal sites require recurrent freshwater flushing sufficient to prevent persistent salt accumulation.
placement.soil: Aerated dead leaves, wood, carcass material or imported organic sediment; exclude vent-contaminated deposits and salt-loaded splash debris.
placement.fog: Supports entrance humidity; deep growth follows local moisture, oxygen and carbon delivery.
placement.density: Patchy colonies bounded by suitable organic deposits. Deep sites require a continuing local aeration route through connected air spaces; coastal sites additionally require freshwater flushing.

generator.seasonal: Fruits after moisture pulses and fresh organic delivery; deep colonies follow substrate inputs rather than sunlight.
generator.wind_response: Low cushions move little; exposed edges dry. Loose spores can disperse in air, while tacky clumps transfer by contact.

journal.en: Pale bread grows on what the cave receives. It smells of fruit, but makes no light.
journal.es: Pan pálido crece sobre lo que recibe la cueva. Huele a fruta, pero no da luz.
